subject: Preflight: VPC cutover gatecheck & sanity sprint (runbook verification)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acmecorp.com>, ops@acmecorp.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Preflight: VPC cutover gatecheck & sanity sprint (runbook verification)

Hi Sam / Acme ops,

As discussed in the call Friday, we're planning the cutover preflight and a short sanity sprint after the VPC routing changes on Wednesday 23rd. Before we move the DNS TTL and start traffic steering, I want to validate the runbook playback and confirm our acceptance criteria for the post-deploy smoke window.

High-level asks:
- Can Acme run the connectivity sweep (TCP/HTTPS + BGP health) and drop the results in the ticket by T-15m? (we'll consume the log attachment format in the checklist)
- Redwood will run the KV-cache priming + sample inference smoke (10 concurrent warm sessions) and validate latency P50/P95 thresholds.
- If telemetry shows >2% 500s or token-error spike, we trigger an automated fallback to the compatible dedicated model variant per policy.

Key runbook snippets attached: redwood_runbook_v2.pdf and smoke_checklist.csv. Topology diagram included for routing references. Please review the acceptance criteria below and confirm:

Acceptance criteria (must all be met):
1) BGP adjacency stable for 5m across primary/backup paths.
2) Firewall rules allow inter-subnet management plane (TCP 22/443) from Acme jump hosts.
3) KV-cache hit rate >= 60% after priming script (see runbook step 4b).
4) P50 generation latency < 120ms, P95 < 350ms for the traced test prompts.
5) Audit/tracing events emitted for the first 1000 requests to the central logging endpoint.

Timeline:
- 22 Jun 18:00 - preflight dry-run (no traffic change)
- 23 Jun 02:00-03:00 - maintenance window (traffic steering + DNS TTL flip)
- 23 Jun 03:00-04:00 - post-deploy sanity sprint and handback

If anything in the runbook or checklist needs to be tightened, call it out here. Otherwise please confirm "Acme ready" and I'll kick off the bridge invite + runbook playback on 23rd.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Private Deployments (Americas)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_runbook_v2.pdf (runbook, 21 pages), smoke_checklist.csv (CSV checklist, 1.2KB), topology-diagram.png (PNG, 420KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Sam Lee <sam.lee@acmecorp.com>, ops@acmecorp.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preflight: VPC cutover gatecheck & sanity sprint (runbook verification)

Thanks Vanessa — quick clarifications from the ops checklist side:

- The KV priming script (runbook step 4b) assumes you will start 12 warm sessions, not 10; I'm updating the CSV to reflect the exact concurrency matrix (attached a new version inline in the checklist).
- On firewall NAT: Acme should ensure ephemeral ports are allowed for return traffic from the inference cluster; otherwise some streaming connections can stall.
- Regarding audit logs: which retention window do we need for this smoke? The SOC2 evidence packet requires logs for the first 24h of the cutover. If Acme can't forward that to our central collector, we need a tarball of the raw wire logs within 6h.

One potential failure mode to call out: if BGP flaps and the KV priming fails mid-run, the fallback to the dedicated variant should be immediate but the runbook currently leaves manual confirmation. I recommend we change that to automatic fallback with a 3-min cooldown to avoid cascading latency spikes. Karthik — can you weigh in on whether the automatic fallback is safe for Acme's traffic pattern?

Marissa
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Vanessa / team,

Acme ops confirms the following:
- We'll run the connectivity sweep and upload acme-connectivity-scan.log to the Jira ticket (OPS-4829) by T-15m. Expect the scan to include BGP adjacency checks and traceroutes from our edge to the Redwood ingress IPs.
- Logs: we can forward syslog/flow logs to your collector for the first 24h. If you prefer a tarball, we can provide that on a 4h cadence.
- Automatic fallback: we prefer an automatic fallback to the dedicated model on detection of >2% 5xxs sustained for 2 minutes, with a manual rollback. The rollback decision should be manual from our side (Acme SRE) to avoid repeated flip-flops.

One ask: can Redwood expose a single stream of per-route token-cost metrics to our billing team for the first 48h? We'll need that to reconcile consumption spikes.

We'll be on the bridge for the dry-run Wednesday evening; attaching the connectivity log as soon as it's finished.

Thanks,
Sam Lee
Platform SRE (AcmeCorp)

Attachment: acme-connectivity-scan.log (4.8MB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sam Lee <sam.lee@acmecorp.com>, ops@acmecorp.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preflight: VPC cutover gatecheck & sanity sprint (runbook verification)

Thanks all — quick operational decision and signoff from my side:

1) Automatic fallback: we will enable automatic fallback as proposed but with two safeguards: a) a 2-minute sustained error window (Acme requested 2 minutes) and b) an automated cooldown of 3 minutes after a fallback before attempting to return traffic. That prevents flip-flops.
2) KV priming concurrency: set to 12 warm sessions (Marissa updated the checklist). The priming script will emit a KV-cache-hit-rate metric that the console will alert on if <55% after 10 minutes.
3) Logs/retention: Redwood will accept forwarded logs to our collector for 24h; if anything is missing, Acme will provide the tarball within 6h.
4) Billing stream: I will open a short-lived metric export to Acme's billing team for 48h and provide a temporary read-only token.

Go/No-Go criteria for the bridge (we'll evaluate these live during the dry-run):
- Go: all preflight connectivity checks green, KV cache hit >= 55%, P50 < 150ms on priming trace, and no sustained 5xx spikes.
- No-Go: BGP not stable for 5m, firewall blocking management plane, or telemetry pipeline lag > 60s.

If we see No-Go during the dry-run, we'll stop and adjust runbook steps, then re-run the dry playback. If Go, we proceed with the window on 23 Jun and run the sanity sprint.

Marking this thread as "ready for dry-run" from Redwood ops. Sam — thanks for the scan; please post the log to OPS-4829 when available.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
